transport: RS-485 side is vendor-documented: RJ45, powered from the port at 5 V ±0.5 V, 115200 bps 8N1 (WiFi 2.4G RJ45 D manual v1.3 and datasheet; BLE RJ45 A manual v1.2 gives 2400-115200 bps, default 115200). eBox-WIFI-01 datasheet: 300 bps-230400 bps, default 115200. The LAN/BLE side is NOT documented by any vendor paper in hand — no TCP port, no GATT service or characteristic UUIDs, no framing.
blocks: None of its own. These are transparent bridges, not Modbus slaves — whatever map the attached controller or inverter has is what you get, unchanged.

refutedOnReview: Refuted on every axis, including by its own evidence field, which states these devices "have no register map to share" — so a dialect entry (which by the skill's definition means matching register addresses) must not exist for them.  1. No register map in any cited source. I extracted all five committed PDFs at /Users/lemarier/dev/solar/docs/ and counted keywords: epever-ebox-wifi-01-datasheet-v1.0.pdf, epever-wifi-2
gotchas: eBox-WIFI-01: one community Home Assistant configuration reaches it as Modbus RTU-over-TCP on port 8088 (gabrielpc1190/Home-Assistant_EPEver-eBox-Wifi-01-MODBUS). That is community-single — a GitHub code search turned up no second independent implementation using the same port. Do not commit it to a config default; con

The BLE adapters are one-to-one only (BLE RJ45 A manual v1.2: 'the Bluetooth module only supports one-to-one communication'), and the BLE RJ45 D manual states it supports Offline Mode only. A phone app connected to the dongle is a client holding the only slot.
The WiFi 2.4G RJ45 D manual says the adapter works only with EPEver's own Solar Guardian app. That is a cloud path, not a local API, and is the opposite of what a cabin gateway needs.

All of these draw their 5 V from pins 1/2 of the controller's RJ45 — the same pins the v2.5 protocol document warns must never be used by a host cable ('Do not use the Vcc pins (+5v), or the controller may be damaged permanently'). A dongle and a USB-RS485 adapter on the same bus via a naive splitter is the failure mod

A plain USB-to-RS485 cable (CC-USB-RS485-150U, also sold at The Cabin Depot) sidesteps this whole category and keeps the map at epever-tracer-a. That is the cheap path and the one already taken by cabin-epever.
unmappedReports: None of these expose readings of their own in any documented way. If a driver ever wraps one as DeviceKind gateway, the obvious metrics — link-online, uptime — exist in the contract already, but nothing published says the device reports them.
